label: Heavy, with openings
summary: A heavy day with narrow openings. Iran's deputy foreign minister said the Strait of Hormuz remains closed despite a temporary Oman transit deal, while Trump warned any new mining would see ships destroyed. Ukrainian drones set Russia's fourth-largest refinery ablaze, yet the Pope's envoy met Sergei Lavrov — the first Vatican-Moscow talks since 2022. Rebels killed 27 in Sudan's South Kordofan, the UN said Myanmar's rights situation had hit a new low, and a nursery fire at Islamabad's main hospital killed 15 newborns. Markets were the calm spot: Asian stocks rose as oil extended declines. Medicine supplied the clearest good news — a world-first central retina transplant restored a woman's sight, and US regulators approved the first drug targeting narcolepsy's cause. No editorial adjustment.
